gen-gf-jim-nightshade-fs-epilogue: Epilogue draws its curvy, unclamped letters from a wire-thin monoline skeleton, a sans-serif that suits brief reading rather than endless paragraphs. Jim Nightshade earns its place big and short.
gen-gf-jim-nightshade-fs-public-sans: Scrawled and dark, Jim Nightshade packs close-set, uniform-stroke letters into a heavy texture. Public Sans steps in with a hefty lowercase and broad counters, a trustworthy sans that sits comfortably in modest bites.
gen-gf-jim-nightshade-work-sans: Work Sans keeps its c tips apart and its mean line set high. Jim Nightshade brings casual, close-set scrawl up top, and the body is made for dipping in briefly, not settling down for hours.
gen-gf-julee-fs-fira-sans: Friendly and hand-drawn, Julee presses its letters into tight, cable-like bundles, while Fira Sans swings its s curves wide. Scribble meets clarity here, and it is built for brief reading.
gen-gf-julee-manrope: Tight, friendly and hand-drawn, Julee looks a lot like bundled cable. Save Julee for big, brief lines and let Manrope handle the gentle reading with bright, open curves and a single-width stroke.
gen-gf-kavivanar-fs-amulya: Loose and friendly, Kavivanar writes at a constant stroke with a flaring, open s, like a quick note jotted down. Amulya, a modern sans-serif with generous curves, is gentle going in modest doses.
gen-gf-kavivanar-outfit: Outfit bends its cable-like curves and stops them short of closing, an approachable sans meant for brief reading. Kavivanar keeps a constant, hand-drawn stroke up front, so the two feel like one loose, friendly voice.
gen-gf-klee-one-fs-amulya: Graceful and hand-written, Klee One cuts its terminals well short. Let Amulya, a modern sans with generous curves, run slightly larger, since it works for just a few lines.
gen-gf-klee-one-fs-neco: Klee One writes with a stylus-like, fixed-pressure line and gracefully clipped terminals. Neco, a dignified serif with a measured swell from hairline to stem, carries a few lines with authority.
gen-gf-klee-one-fs-plein: Graceful, uniform strokes and clipped terminals give Klee One its handwritten charm. Use it large and brief, then let Plein, a reliable sans-serif with clear channels into round letters, handle modest bites of text.
